newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks close up despite interest rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks close up despite interest rate rise.

text.p: Blue chip stocks led Caracas stocks higher in light trade despite a rise in interest rates, brokers said.
"Trade was light but prices firmed generally after hitting support levels," said independent broker Freddy Zambrano.

The market's leading index gained 1.03 percent to close at 6,229.82 points, even though interest rates, as measured by yields on benchmark six month Central Bank TEMS, rose 158 basis points to 15.00 percent.
Among traded issues, 33 rose, five fell and nine closed flat as a total of 17.5 million stocks changed hands, worth three billion bolivars ($6.4 million).

"Blue chips led the rise, despite the Christmas lethargy," said one trader, adding that investors had been cheered by news late Tuesday that Thursday's auction of Banco de Venezuela and Banco Consolidado would be going ahead.

Telephone company CANTV rose 40.00 bolivars to end at 1820.00, utility Electricidad de Caracas gained 9.00 bolivars to close at 532.00, and foods company Mavesa gained 4.00 bolivars to finish at 147.00 bolivars.
